extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals and communications teams producing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for choosing, creating, and delivering images, video, infographics, and slides to include in press releases so they increase engagement, journalist pickup, and shareability while avoiding legal or technical pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use visuals to boost engagement and reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Include visual content because it gets shared more and drives better results (engagement, shares, views, media pickup, conversions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual content boosts engagement (e.g., Facebook posts with images get 53% more likes and 104% more comments); tweets with images are nearly twice as likely to be retweeted; content with images can get 94% more views and press releases with visuals see up to 9.7x more views. Journalists prefer press releases with visuals, increasing chances of coverage, and visual content converts more effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep visuals relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Use images/videos only if they add value to your story and are relevant to the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't overwhelm your press release with images. Use visuals especially for visually-driven topics like product launches. If you don't have suitable visuals, a logo can be a good alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit quantity to avoid overwhelm
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid overloading the release with too many images or galleries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include images that add value; too many visuals can dilute the story. (Note: some platforms like Prezly don't limit number of images, but editorial judgment still applies.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure copyright compliance and proper licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use images without permission; use your own graphics, properly licensed stock, or get permission from the creator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid legal and PR issues by using owned content, stock photos with proper licenses, or explicit permission from original creators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sending large attachments in email pitches
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't attach big image files to pitch emails; provide accessible download/viewing instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never send large image attachments via email. Use a press release platform (e.g., Prezly) that allows easy viewing and downloading of high-quality images to prevent inbox clutter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize visuals for mobile viewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure images, infographics, slides and videos display well and load quickly on mobile devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many journalists access press releases on their phones. Ensure images are mobile-friendly and load quickly across devices for a smooth user experience; make infographics and slides easy to read on small screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose visuals that tell a story
rubrics_metrics.description: Select visuals that complement and enhance the narrative of the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick images that support your key points and help communicate the intended impression; visuals should help grab attention and make the story more engaging. (See link to storytelling in business.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Label images with descriptive filenames and alt text
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide descriptive file names and alt text for images to help journalists and search engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive filenames and alt text improve SEO and make it easier for reporters to understand and use your images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep videos short and simple
rubrics_metrics.description: Make video content brief and to the point to maintain audience engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overcomplicating the story in video form — short, simple videos work best and can be filmed on a smartphone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host videos on reliable platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload videos to established platforms (e.g., YouTube, Wistia) instead of self-hosting large video files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosting on services like YouTube or Wistia helps with load speed, SEO, and social sharing; avoid hosting large files on your own server.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use video to simplify complex ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage video for demos, tutorials, or explanations that are hard to convey in text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Videos are especially good at explaining product demos or tutorials and can make complicated concepts accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage video for emotional impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Use video to create an emotional connection and make your message memorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Video is one of the most effective ways to engage the audience emotionally, increasing recall and interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vertical video for social platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Format video vertically for Instagram, TikTok and other mobile-first social platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For social sharing and better engagement on platforms like Instagram and TikTok, use vertical video to optimize viewing experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design infographics around a single main message
rubrics_metrics.description: Create infographics that focus on one primary takeaway and make data visually digestible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with the question 'What impression do I want the reader to take away from this data?' Design around that answer; keep it simple and focused on one main message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use high-quality visuals that match brand style
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure infographics and images match your brand aesthetic and are professionally presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality visuals aligned with brand style increase credibility and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit text in infographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep text minimal so the data and visuals remain the focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit text to make the data the star and improve readability and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make infographics mobile-friendly and readable
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure infographics are legible and usable on small screens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for mobile readability; test how charts and labels render on phones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share infographics on appropriate social platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute infographics on platforms like Pinterest to boost reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage platform-specific audiences (e.g., Pinterest for visual content) to increase distribution and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create compelling slide decks with a strong cover
rubrics_metrics.description: Use slides to summarize key points; start with a compelling cover slide featuring a strong PR headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the cover slide attention-grabbing and clearly communicate the core message to entice viewers to continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep slides clean and visually engaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid clutter on slides; prioritize clear visuals and concise messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design slides to be visually appealing and easy to scan; avoid overloading slides with text or busy graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include links and sources in slides
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide links to relevant sources or additional information within slide decks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including links helps journalists and readers find more context and follow-up information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed slides in press release or website for easy access
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider embedding slide decks in the release or on your website to make them easy to view and share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding removes friction for journalists and audiences who want to view or download the slides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share slide decks on SlideShare to boost visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SlideShare (and similar platforms) to distribute and increase traffic for slide content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing slides on SlideShare can drive more traffic and make the content discoverable by a wider audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a backlog of visuals by capturing content routinely
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it a habit to take photos and video during regular work activities to create a library of usable visuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you carry a smartphone, snap pictures and film footage throughout the workday to create a solid backlog with minimal extra effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage internal talent for DIY visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask colleagues with photography or social media skills to contribute visuals or help create content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify budding photographers or TikTok-savvy team members to reuse internal skills rather than always outsourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use affordable tools to create visuals in-house
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ user-friendly tools (PowerPoint, Keynote, Canva, Placeit, Jenny AI, Adobe Audition, Wistia) to produce images, infographics, slides, and videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools let non-designers create professional visuals; use templates and platform features to speed production and stay on budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outsource when time/resources are limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Hire external services for infographics, video, or design when you lack time or in-house capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options range by budget and speed: Visual.ly for turnkey infographics/videos, 99designs for crowdsourced designs, Fiverr for low-cost tasks, and Unsplash for royalty-free images. Outsourcing doesn't have to be expensive but choose vendors based on quality/timeframe needs.
